title: Terraform-provisioned Multisignal VPC Guardian (adaptive token throughput + latency/error SLO fusion)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Private/VPC customers run inference at variable token rates and often see incidents where token saturation and transient latency spikes coincide with elevated error rates. Existing probes are siloed (latency-only, error-only, synthetic TPS probes) and are deployed separately via ad-hoc modules. This work bundles a Terraform-driven module + operator configuration that deploys a fused, multimodal health 'Guardian' for each VPC edge worker fleet. Goal: deploy a single, opinionated probe mesh (latency quantiles, error-rate windows, token throughput sliding windows) that evaluates a combined SLO signal and triggers tiered remediation: alerts, automated token-backoff, and canary-aware deployment gates. The Guardian will be provisioned via Terraform modules so infra teams can opt-in per VPC with consistent defaults and override knobs.
scope: In scope: Terraform module to provision probe configs, RBAC roles, and Prometheus scrape/service monitors; operator-side config (probe CRD templates) and runtime fusion logic; alerting rules and PagerDuty/Slack actions; Canary gate hooks to IaC pipelines; dashboards and runbook. Out of scope: model-level token accounting within customer model runtime (separate agent), long-term retention changes.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module at modules/vpc_guardian produces idempotent resources (ServiceMonitor, ConfigMap, RBAC) and is covered by unit tests
Guardian operator accepts a VPC config and deploys probes for latency (p50/p95/p99), error-rate (1m/5m windows), and token-throughput (rolling 30s/5m) for each edge worker set
SLO fusion engine computes a composite health score and exposes a 1m/5m health metric that can be used in alerting and rollout gates
Canary gate library integrated into IaC pipeline refuses a rollout when composite health degrades past configured threshold during canary window
Dashboard with focused panels for composite health, constituent signals, and token flow visualizations is available in Grafana link
End-to-end e2e test simulating burst traffic verifies automated backoff and alerting without manual intervention

technical_notes: Probe types: latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99 via histogram buckets), error-rate counters (5xx and 4xx), token throughput counters (tokens emitted per second, per worker, exported via /metrics).
Fusion approach: sliding-window z-score normalization of each signal, then a weighted sum where weights are customer-configurable. Default weights: latency 0.45, errors 0.35, throughput 0.20.
Thresholding: composite health score > 0.7 => WARN, > 0.9 => CRITICAL. Hysteresis windows: enter/exit thresholds to avoid flapping.

Automated remediation: 1) soft backoff (reduce per-request concurrency / increase batching) 2) if still CRITICAL, shed non-essential routes and escalate to on-call. Backoff control uses per-vpc config applied through runtime API.
TF module outputs: guardian_config_map, service_monitor_name, alert_rule_ids, dashboard_url. Module accepts override for weights and thresholds.
Security: probe metrics contain token-rate numeric aggregates only (no PII), metrics export uses mTLS to internal prometheus, RBAC limited to monitoring namespace.
Compatibility: supports private deployments running runtime-1.18+ and requires guardian-operator 0.9.0+ on the cluster.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): deploy module to staging VPC and validate metrics and dashboards - 1 week
Stage 2 (canary customers): enable for 2 low-traffic private customers, run 72-hour soak with canary gate enabled - 2 weeks
Stage 3 (gradual rollout): opt-in in Dedicated test fleets and customer pilot cohorts - 4 weeks
Stage 4 (GA): default deploy in new VPCs and make available as opt-in flag for existing ones
tests: unit: terraform plan tests for module inputs/outputs
integration: operator deploy + probe registration in kind cluster
e2e: simulated token storm that triggers soft backoff and verifies traffic shaping
canary: pipeline job that runs a synthetic traffic profile during tf-apply to validate canary gating
risks: False positives from transient downstream latency could trigger unnecessary backoff and customer-visible degradations
RBAC or metrics misconfiguration could expose internal counters if not reviewed
Performance overhead from high-cardinality probe labels on very large fleets
Canary gate failure could block legitimate rollouts if thresholds are too strict
mitigations: Start conservative default thresholds and tuned hysteresis; allow opt-in aggressive mode
Security review and automated linting of TF module to ensure no secrets are output
Limit probe label cardinality by aggregating to pool-level metrics rather than per-host by default
Add manual override path with explicit approval to bypass canary gate for emergency fixes
